notes:
A three-order delivery run, all of it inside Windurst Waters. The unnumbered preamble is a genuine precondition and not a step: if Kerutoto keeps talking about challenging Diabolos you must first accept Waking Dreams, and nothing in the packets can see that state.

The page says 'talk to the following NPCs in this exact order', but read as a player would, that sentence covers 'to RECEIVE this quest' -- bullets 1 and 2, which really are ordered, since Ohbiru-Dohbiru has to complain before Kerutoto will hand the quest over. Beyond that the page contradicts a strict ladder itself: bullet 3 asks two NPCs with an '&' and no order, and the closing line says each item traded nets its own portion of the 1,000 gil, so the three trades settle independently. Bullets 3 and 4-6 are therefore two unordered groups; a strict ladder would mark Ohbiru-Dohbiru and then sit there until you happened to visit him first.

Bullet 7 is NOT a step -- its own (!UPDATE!) retracts it: 'No need to speak with Kerutoto. The quest will be automatically completed once you trade the final orders.' So this quest has no hand-in and none is invented.

No evidence anywhere. Every item involved is an ordinary tradable food; holding a Grilled Hare proves you shopped, not that you delivered, and none of the three NPCs grants a key item.

Kerutoto's position is the one real conflict: the header puts him in Windurst Waters South at (J-8), bullet 2 sends you to the NORTHERN Rhinostery building. The header's grid is kept because it is the identity-bound field, and the walkthrough's wording is recorded in the note. The page never gives Kenapa-Keppa a location at all, so his steps carry the quest's zone and no grid.

notes:
The resolver settled what the page could not. The wiki's Reward block lists both 'Watercraft' and '"Watercrafting"' and the walkthrough talks about receiving 'the Watercraft' mid-quest; res/items.lua has no Watercraft at all, while res/key_items.lua has 2167 'watercraft' (the portable boat) and 2205 '"Watercrafting"' -- name INCLUDING the literal quote marks, which is why the unquoted spelling resolves to nothing. So the boat you are handed at bullet 2 is a KEY ITEM and it is recorded as one.

That makes this the rare quest where a Reward-listed thing really is mid-quest evidence: bullet 2's own sub-bullet shouts 'You are not done with the quest yet! You still need the "Watercrafting" Key Item.' Hard rule 7 exists because a reward proves the quest is over; here the page states outright that it does not. It is used as step 2's evidence and flagged evidence_is_reward so the demotion is applied by the validator rather than hidden. '"Watercrafting"' itself IS the completion reward and is deliberately not evidence anywhere.

Bullets 3 and 4 are two separate crossings, not one: you cast the boat at the south side of (I-7), land on the southern island at (J-9), walk to the WEST side of (J-9) and cast again to reach the north bank. Each is its own step in its own place, and each carries the Watercraft as a held requirement. The 'dive right in' sub-bullet earns the unique Toxin Tussler title and the page says it may be done after the quest is over, so it is a note and not an optional step -- there is nothing to target.

Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the addon's nine regions, so the region gates nothing; the FLevel 1 and the raw string are kept.

notes:
A map quest that ends on a ??? with no hand-in, so none is invented.

Bullet 1 comes BEFORE the giver: you read a diary on the second floor of a house at (G-7) in Southern San d'Oria -- note the zone, the header's (G-7) is Port San d'Oria and the two only look alike. The page names the object only 'the diary', which is a common noun and not a name -- exactly the 'the baskets' case hard rule 1 describes -- so the target is left unnamed and untyped rather than promoted to 'Diary'. The step keeps its rung and simply carries no marker. If the live object does turn out to have a name, it is missing here and must come from a reading of the game, not from this page.

Bullet 3 is a real OR across two zones -- Moblin Ashman/Moblin Gurneyman in Oldton Movalpolos, or Moblin Groundman in Newton Movalpolos -- and a step has one zone. Oldton is recorded because the page leads with it; Newton is in the note and the branch is flagged. The Moblin Hotrok is the one observable thing in the quest and sits on that step.

Bullets 4, 5 and 6 do not agree with each other. [4] says climb to the TOP where Jormungand spawns, [5] puts a slope at (F-9) leading all the way DOWN to the zone entrance, [6] says fall down the Southern Slope you see as soon as you zone. Read as a player would, they are one descent from the zone line to a ledge, so they are one travel step and the disagreement is recorded rather than reconciled -- it is why this quest is medium.

Bullets 7 and 8 are kept apart because they need different things of you: examine the ??? with empty hands, then trade the Hotrok to it. Neither can carry a marker. The Map of the Uleguerand Range is the Reward and is not evidence.

notes:
A clean six-rung investigation with nothing observable in it: no key item is ever handed over and the Elixir is the Reward, so every evidence field is null and the ladder runs on the session latch alone. That is the honest answer here -- reaching for the Elixir would put the mark on the last step the moment one dropped from anywhere else.

The header writes the giver 'Gentle Tiger' and the walkthrough writes 'Gentle Tiger (S)'. The (S) form is the one recorded, because the resolver folds it to BOTH 'gentle tiger [s]' and 'gentle tiger' -- a superset of what the bare name gives -- so it can only help. The header string is preserved verbatim in start.raw.

The unnumbered Notice above bullet 1 is a real gate and not a step: one game day plus a re-zone after Light in the Darkness, neither of which any packet reports. Bullet 3's sub-bullets are transport options and bullet 4's is a warning about four Orcs; both stay as notes.

Bullet 6 gives Blatherix only a grid, (F-8), and no zone. The walkthrough has not left Bastok Markets (S) since bullet 5, so that is the zone recorded, and the inference is stated here rather than buried. The closing line about returning to Cait Sith (Mission) belongs to the mission line, not to this quest.

notes:
The header's Start field is EMPTY, which is not a defect -- this quest genuinely has no giver. Bullet 1 begins it by zoning into Batallia Downs (S) from Jugner Forest (S), so start.npc stays null, start.zone is recovered from the walkthrough, and start.raw keeps the empty header. The quest survives that because bullets 2 and 3 both name markable entities: validate.py only fails a quest with no start NPC when no step is markable either.

The Bulwark Gate at Sauromugue Champaign (S) (E-6) is examined TWICE, before and after the errand, and both examinations are kept -- they are the same object but not the same moment, and the second one is what the pot is for. The page never says outright that you must be holding the Pot of martial relish for the second examination; that it is the whole point of bullet 3 is plain enough to record as a held requirement, and it is what lets the ladder tell the two visits apart.

The Pot of martial relish is the quest's only usable evidence, on step 3 where it is granted. The [KI] Large memory fragment at bullet 5 is deliberately NOT evidence twice over: it is the header's Reward, and its name is not unique in res/key_items.lua, so the resolver rejects it rather than guess an id.

All the sub-bullets are transport advice except the one naming Amalasanda in the Tenshodo at Lower Jeuno (J-8) as the source of the three ingredients -- a shop, not a step.

notes:
Four bullets, two steps. Bullet 3 is an OUTCOME -- 'You will receive Soul gem clasp and access to the level 95 cap fight' -- and bullet 4 says outright 'This quest is now technically completed', so neither is a step; a verb scan would have made two out of them. Bullet 3's sub-bullet about saying 'Yes' when Atori-Tutori asks if you are ready is part of the cutscene the trade fires, not a separate NPC to visit, and the page itself says it does not start the BCNM. The other sub-bullet is a re-buy price after a loss.

Bullet 2 folds the fetch into the trade rather than getting its own obtain rung: the Seasoning Stone drops from 'nearly all level 90+ regular monsters outside of Abyssea', which names no mob and gives no place, so an obtain step would be an unmarkable rung whose only content -- hold a Seasoning Stone -- the trade step already carries as a requirement.

Steps 1 and 2 are consecutive on the same NPC, which is one marker with readiness looking ahead across both, exactly as intended. 'Nomad Moogle' is on the resolver's ambiguous list, so the Ru'Lude Gardens zone MUST stay on both steps or the whole quest is demoted; it does. The Soul gem clasp is a key item but it is also the header's Reward, so it is not evidence -- this quest carries none.

The After the walkthrough 'Lore' section is a spoiler table about Atori-Tutori and Beat Around the Bushin. No steps in it.

The opponent is your own Adventuring Fellow. The page never gives it a monster name -- the table lists the job it will take depending on yours, not what it is called -- so the fight step records no mob rather than inventing one. That table is reference material and produces no steps at all.

Quest Reqs are Familiarity level 100+ and Adventuring Fellow level 61+. Neither has a slot in the schema and neither is observable from packets, so they gate nothing and are flagged. Bullet 1's sub-bullet -- if Luto gives no cutscene, try Ajahkeem -- is a genuine alternative giver that the schema has no way to express on a step, so only Luto is recorded and the fallback lives in the note.

The remaining sub-bullets (fellow job table, no XP loss, damage capped near 200 per hit) are all commentary.

notes:
A short repeatable delivery, entirely inside Abyssea - Uleguerand. The whole quest turns on one key item: the Torch coal, granted by the Coal Casket behind Zauko, which is step 2's evidence and the held requirement on both deliveries.

The two outlying caskets are an unordered group, and the page is what says so: the sub-bullet under bullet 5 explains that if the coal is destroyed you 'acquire it again then return to the missed one' and that you 'do not have to do both with the same coal' -- which only makes sense if either casket can be the one you still owe. A strict ladder would mark Conflux #6 and refuse to acknowledge #7 until you had gone back.

The coal is destroyed by USING a conflux, which is why the page insists you walk between encampments; that is a real constraint the addon cannot see and is recorded as a note rather than pretended away.

The page gives a grid only for Zauko, (K-9). The two outlying caskets are described only as 'near Conflux #6' and 'near Conflux #7', so their steps carry the zone and no grid -- which does mean their marker will match any Coal Casket in the zone, including the one behind Zauko. That is a real limit of a page that never numbers its own map.

Fame 'aule' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing; the raw string and FLevel 1 are kept. Repeatable is Yes, and the closing line -- zoning is required to repeat -- is a cooldown, not a step.

steps.note: at the first encampment, near Conflux #5
the casket directly behind Zauko

third encampment, near Conflux #7, again with no grid given. Order between this and the Conflux #6 casket is free -- lose the coal and you fetch another and return to whichever you missed.
Conflux #7 warps you back to #5 for the reward -- the coal is already spent by now, so the conflux is safe. Zoning is required before the quest can be repeated.
